newsitem.title: ITALY: Marzotto to make cash call for HPI merger.
newsitem.headline: Marzotto to make cash call for HPI merger.

text.p: Italian textiles group Marzotto intends a 3.61 billion lire capital increase as part of its operations to merge with newly formed Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI), a statement from the groups said.
The capital increase is to cover warrants to be allotted on the basis of one warrant for every 20 Marzotto shares of any class currently in issue.
These warrants may be exercised to subscribe for one ordinary share per warrant at a price of 7,000 per share, which approximately corresponds to consolidated net equity per share, it said.
This would result in the creation of up to 3,609,415 ordinary shares providing a total additional capital of 25.3 billion lire, it said.

HPI, which has just completed its spin-off from financial holding Gemina, and Marzotto said this weekend they intend to merge to form Gruppo Industriale Marzotto, which they said will be one of the largest textile and clothing groups in the world.

"Prior to the merger, Marzotto will also spin off its own operating businesses into wholly owned subsidiaries and will become an industrial holding. It will subsequently change its corporate purpose to reflect this new role," it said.
Marzotto planned an extraordinary general meeting to approve the operations before the merger.
